concepts.name: Global Pressure Belt Distribution and Thermal vs. Dynamic Origin
key_dimensions: Distinction between thermally induced belts (equatorial low, polar high) vs. dynamically induced belts (subtropical high, subpolar low)
Why subtropical high is NOT caused by surface heating — UPSC trap on equating all highs with cold conditions
Seasonal shifting of pressure belts with apparent movement of the Sun (ITCZ migration)
Consequences of belt shifting on regional climates (e.g., Mediterranean, Savanna)

concepts.name: Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ): Nature, Migration, and Climatic Significance
key_dimensions: ITCZ as a low-pressure trough vs. a fixed equatorial belt — distinction between dynamic reality and simplified model
Asymmetric migration: ITCZ shifts more into northern hemisphere (land-dominated) than southern hemisphere
Role of ITCZ in triggering South Asian and West African monsoons
ITCZ vs. Equatorial Trough vs. Doldrums — overlapping but non-identical concepts (UPSC trap)

concepts.name: Subtropical High Pressure Belt (Horse Latitudes): Formation, Characteristics, and Desert Link
key_dimensions: Dynamic origin via subsidence of Hadley Cell — NOT thermal cooling
Why subtropical highs are stronger and more persistent over oceans than continents
Subtropical highs as the source region of both Trade Winds and Westerlies
Connection between subtropical highs and location of hot deserts (western coasts of continents at 20°–30°)

concepts.name: Hadley Cell: Structure, Mechanism, and Asymmetry
key_dimensions: Three-cell model: Hadley, Ferrel, and Polar cells — which are thermally direct vs. thermally indirect
Ferrel Cell as thermally INDIRECT (driven by adjacent cells) — a classic UPSC trap
Hadley Cell's role in moisture transport and ITCZ maintenance
Seasonal strengthening of Hadley Cell and its link to monsoon intensity

concepts.name: Trade Winds: Direction, Consistency, and Oceanographic Significance
key_dimensions: Northeast Trades (NH) vs. Southeast Trades (SH) — Coriolis deflection direction trap
Trade winds as the most consistent planetary winds — reason (subtropical high permanence)
Role in driving equatorial ocean currents and upwelling on eastern coasts
Trade Wind Inversion — a stable layer that suppresses rainfall on eastern sides of subtropical oceans (e.g., Atacama)

concepts.name: Westerlies: Variable Nature, Storm Tracks, and Southern Hemisphere Intensity
key_dimensions: Why Westerlies are stronger and more consistent in Southern Hemisphere (Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, Screaming Sixties) — absence of large landmasses
Westerlies as the dominant wind system for mid-latitude cyclone movement
Jet streams embedded within Westerlies — connection between surface winds and upper-air circulation
Westerlies bringing orographic rainfall to western coasts of continents (e.g., Western Europe, Pacific NW)

concepts.name: Polar Easterlies and Polar High: Characteristics and Distinction from Other Highs
key_dimensions: Polar high as THERMALLY induced (cold, dense air) vs. subtropical high (dynamically induced) — critical distinction
Polar Easterlies meeting Westerlies at the Polar Front — creation of subpolar low
Why polar high over Antarctica is stronger and more persistent than Arctic polar high
Polar vortex and its disruption causing extreme cold outbreaks in mid-latitudes

concepts.name: Subpolar Low Pressure Belt: Formation at Polar Front and Cyclogenesis
key_dimensions: Subpolar low as a zone of CONVERGENCE between Westerlies and Polar Easterlies
Dynamic origin via frontal uplift, NOT thermal heating — contrast with equatorial low
Role as the breeding ground for mid-latitude (extratropical) cyclones
Icelandic Low and Aleutian Low as semi-permanent subpolar lows — their seasonal intensification

concepts.name: Coriolis Force and Wind Deflection: Ferrel's Law and UPSC Trap Scenarios
key_dimensions: Deflection to the RIGHT in NH and LEFT in SH — and why it is zero at equator (no Coriolis near ITCZ)
Coriolis force is proportional to wind speed and latitude — implications for wind belt boundaries
Buys Ballot's Law: relationship between pressure gradient and wind direction
Common trap: Coriolis does NOT cause winds, only deflects them — pressure gradient is the primary cause

concepts.name: Jet Streams: Types, Location, and Influence on Surface Weather
key_dimensions: Polar Jet Stream vs. Subtropical Jet Stream — altitude, latitude, and seasonal behavior differences
Western Disturbances as mid-latitude cyclones steered by the Subtropical Westerly Jet into India
Somali Jet (Low-Level Jet) and its role in intensifying the Southwest Monsoon — contrast with upper-level jets
Jet stream meandering (Rossby Waves) and its link to blocking highs, prolonged droughts, and floods

concepts.name: Monsoon Winds: Pressure Reversal Mechanism vs. ITCZ Theory
key_dimensions: Classical thermal theory (differential heating of land and sea) vs. modern ITCZ/jet stream theory of monsoon origin
Role of Mascarene High (subtropical high over southern Indian Ocean) in driving Indian SW Monsoon
Somali Jet as a cross-equatorial flow — how Trade Winds of SH transform into SW Monsoon winds
UPSC trap: Monsoon is NOT simply a sea breeze — it involves large-scale pressure belt shifts and jet dynamics

concepts.name: Land and Sea Breezes: Mechanism, Scale, and Distinction from Monsoon
key_dimensions: Diurnal (daily) cycle vs. seasonal cycle of monsoon — scale distinction critical for UPSC
Sea breeze during day (land heats faster) vs. land breeze at night — specific pressure and temperature dynamics
Why sea breezes can penetrate 50–100 km inland in some regions
Land and sea breezes as local winds — not to be confused with planetary or secondary wind systems

concepts.name: Mountain and Valley Breezes: Anabatic and Katabatic Winds
key_dimensions: Anabatic (valley to mountain, daytime) vs. Katabatic (mountain to valley, nighttime) — direction trap
Katabatic winds at large scale: Bora (Adriatic), Mistral (France), and Antarctic katabatic winds
Role of katabatic winds in frost formation and their impact on viticulture and agriculture
Distinction between katabatic (thermally driven downslope) and Foehn/Chinook (orographic, adiabatic warming)

concepts.name: Foehn and Chinook Winds: Orographic Precipitation and Rain Shadow Effect
key_dimensions: Mechanism: windward side cooling at SALR, leeward side warming at DALR — net temperature gain
Foehn (Alps) vs. Chinook (Rockies) — same mechanism, different geographies
Rain shadow deserts created by this mechanism: Patagonia (behind Andes), Thar (partially behind Western Ghats)
UPSC trap: Chinook called 'Snow Eater' — rapid snowmelt implications for agriculture and flooding

concepts.name: Local Hot and Dry Winds: Loo, Sirocco, Harmattan, and Santa Ana
key_dimensions: Loo (India/Pakistan): hot, dry westerly in summer over Indo-Gangetic Plain — health and agriculture impact
Sirocco (Mediterranean from Sahara) vs. Harmattan (West Africa, desiccating but relatively cooler) — contrast
Santa Ana (California): offshore katabatic wind — link to wildfire risk
Common UPSC trap: Harmattan sometimes called 'Doctor Wind' for its drying, fever-reducing effect in West Africa

concepts.name: El Niño and Southern Oscillation (ENSO): Pressure Reversal and Walker Circulation
key_dimensions: Walker Circulation as an east-west atmospheric circulation driven by Pacific pressure gradient (Darwin vs. Tahiti)
El Niño: weakening/reversal of Trade Winds → warm water moves east → suppressed upwelling off Peru
Southern Oscillation Index (SOI): negative SOI = El Niño, positive SOI = La Niña
ENSO teleconnections: Indian monsoon failure during El Niño, Australian droughts, Peruvian floods — multi-region impact

concepts.name: Rossby Waves (Planetary Waves): Upper Atmosphere Circulation and Surface Weather Link
key_dimensions: Rossby Waves as long-wavelength meanders in the Polar Jet Stream driven by land-sea temperature contrasts and topography
Role in meridional (north-south) heat exchange between tropics and poles
Amplified Rossby Waves linked to 'blocking' patterns causing persistent extreme weather (European heat waves, Indian floods)
UPSC relevance: climate change causing Arctic amplification → wavier jet stream → more extreme events

concepts.name: Pressure Gradient Force, Geostrophic Wind, and Gradient Wind
key_dimensions: Geostrophic wind: balance between pressure gradient force and Coriolis — flows PARALLEL to isobars (upper atmosphere)
Gradient wind: adds centripetal acceleration for curved flow around highs and lows
Surface winds cross isobars at an angle toward low pressure due to friction — angle ~15° over sea, ~30° over land
UPSC trap: upper-level winds are nearly geostrophic; surface winds are NOT — friction breaks geostrophic balance

concepts.name: Convergence and Divergence: Upper Air vs. Surface and Their Role in Cyclone/Anticyclone Maintenance
key_dimensions: Surface convergence + upper-level divergence = LOW pressure system (cyclone) maintenance
Surface divergence + upper-level convergence = HIGH pressure system (anticyclone) maintenance
Why a cyclone dies if upper-level divergence weakens (e.g., tropical cyclone moving over land loses moisture and heat source)
Jet stream exit/entrance regions as zones of preferred upper-level divergence/convergence — cyclogenesis link

concepts.name: Seasonal Pressure Systems: Semi-Permanent Highs and Lows and Their Climatic Controls
key_dimensions: Azores High, Pacific High, Siberian High, Icelandic Low, Aleutian Low — locations and seasonal intensification patterns
Siberian High (winter, thermal) vs. Azores High (year-round, dynamic) — different origins, UPSC trap
How Siberian High drives the Northeast Monsoon over peninsular India and Southeast Asia
UPSC trap: semi-permanent systems are NOT the same as pressure belts — they are localized, seasonally variable centers
